plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large daisy-like flower heads made of yellow ray florets surrounding a dark central disc. Young flower heads track the sun's movement across the sky. Widely cultivated for seed, oil, and ornament, and also found growing wild in prairies and roadsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: North America (native), cultivated worldwide including Ukraine, Russia, Europe, and the United States
plants.funFact: The sunflower head is actually made up of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual flowers arranged in a spiral pattern following the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie plant with drooping pinkish-purple petals around a spiky orange-brown central cone. It is a magnet for bees, butterflies, and goldfinches, and thrives in full sun and tolerates drought.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early fall (June to September)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America; widely grown in gardens in temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The name Echinacea comes from the Greek word 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiny central cone. Native Americans used it medicinally for centuries.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and spikes of fragrant violet-blue flowers. In late summer, the later-blooming varieties are still in flower, while earlier fields are being harvested. It is prized for essential oils, culinary uses, and as a pollinator plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (June to August), with some cultivars lasting into early September
plants.location: Mediterranean region native; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, Tasmania, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: The name lavender comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A striking Australian shrub producing large, crimson, dome-shaped flower heads surrounded by showy red bracts. It blooms at the end of the southern winter and into early spring, when few other plants are flowering, making it important for nectar-feeding birds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (August to November) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, particularly the sandstone ridges around Sydney and the Blue Mountains
plants.funFact: The waratah is the floral emblem of New South Wales, and its name comes from the Aboriginal Eora people's word for the plant. Its flower head is actually a cluster of hundreds of small flowers.
